design.known_asymmetry: Document counts are equal but training word mass is not. Joel has roughly 776-1276 words per fold, David 9525, and Stian 12119.

comparison_to_cross_register_pilot.interpretation: Same-platform training did not rescue Joel's character-based attribution. It improved Joel lexical attribution while redistributing lexical errors to controls. Therefore asymmetric platform/register mismatch was not sufficient to explain the weak character signal.

interpretation.primary_observation: Char-plus-word collapses exactly to the char-only confusion pattern, while word-only has a different pattern and recognizes Joel much better. The surface channels disagree materially.
interpretation.remaining_confound: The equal-document design is severely unequal in words per class because Joel's available Dharma documents are much shorter than control documents. TF-IDF normalizes individual vectors but this does not make the training information content or feature coverage equal across classes.
interpretation.next_test: Repeat the matched-platform folds after deterministically length-normalizing every training and held-out document to a common 50-word window, preserving source-group splits. If character attribution remains poor under equal text budgets, deprioritize surface SVM as an operational calibration target and move to LUAR/content-light controls.
